title: It wasn’t about the fruit.
paragraphs: It wasn’t about the fruit.
It never was.

Eden didn’t collapse because of a bite—
it collapsed because of a belief.

A whisper slithered in:
“Did God really say…?”
And suddenly, trust cracked.

Not hunger.
Not curiosity.
Doubt.
That was the real poison.

Because the moment Eve believed God might be holding out on her,
the fruit stopped being forbidden…
and started looking necessary.
That’s how sin works.

It doesn’t kick the door down.
It questions the Father’s heart.

“You’re missing out.”
“You deserve more.”
“God is limiting you.”

And we fall—not because we’re starving—
but because we stop trusting.
But here’s what we miss…
God didn’t abandon them in the garden.

Right there, in the wreckage of rebellion,
He spoke a promise (Genesis 3:15).

A coming Savior.
A serpent-crusher.
A Redeemer who would bleed to restore what doubt destroyed.
And that’s Jesus.

Where Adam and Eve doubted—
Christ trusted.

Where they reached for the tree—
He died on one.
So now, the real question isn’t about a fruit.
It’s this:
Do you trust God… or the voice that says He’s not enough?
Because every day, that same whisper is still talking.
And every day, grace is still answering.

Come back.
Trust again.
The Father is not withholding from you—He already gave His Son.
